As indicated at the beginning of this section, the basic structures are present to accomplish these programs. It remains up to the leader-ship of the area to make the structure work.
Social impacts, unlike others, cannot be effectively mitigated by pre-arranged contract. The coal developers will provide employment preference and training opportunities for Crow Tribal members. They will, through taxation and royalties paid, provide a financial base which can assist in mitigation programs. Government assistance programs will also assure that certain mitigating measures are maintained. It is, however, up to the various interests within the ommunities and their leadership to conceptualize, plan and implement the required mitigating measures. As indicated, the community planning process has just begun. Whether or not it will be adequate in scope, depth, and timing remains to be seen.
